#### The same document distribution, different parameters {#bowls}

Each circle is one possible complete document. Choose an inner bowl afresh for each document, then draw a circle from it. Initially, every construction produces A, B, and C with probability $1/3$ each. Redraw $\psi$ chooses a new sample for the Bayesian prior $\psi$; every representation then induces that same new $f_\psi$.

The rectangle encloses the representation chips and the whole construction: the diagram determines $\psi$, although different diagrams can determine the same $\psi$. Inside the rectangle, the outer bowl describes $P(\theta_m\mid\psi)$ for a fixed shared $\psi$. Switching representations preserves this $f_\psi=r$. Applied at every $r$ with the law of $f_\psi$ fixed, it also preserves the full document process. Redrawing $\psi$ selects a different example.
